unmapped_findings: For this sample (19Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h), the Vickers hardness is 574.1 ± 8.6 HV (Table 4), a moderate increase over the solution-treated baseline of 263.8 ± 1.1 HV; the aging hardening response of the 19Al alloy at 525 °C is gradual and fails to reach the alloy's peak hardness.

The α→β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy at 525 °C is very slow: the SE-SEM image at 525 °C/3 h shows a uniform α matrix with no visible precipitate, and only ~12.1 % β-Mn forms even after 525 °C/10 h (Fig. 6), the lowest among the three Al contents.
In the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C the small amount of β-Mn that forms precipitates primarily along α grain boundaries, with a smaller amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn within the α grains.
The EDS-measured chemical composition of the 19Al alloy is Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6 and Cu 5.0 at.% (Table 1).
